properties.name: Fujii-dera
properties.description: Temple 11 of the Shikoku 88-temple pilgrimage, one of only three Zen temples on the route. Its ancient wisteria and position at the foot of the Shōsan-ji ascent make it the threshold to the first major Henro-korogashi mountain stage.

properties.name: HENRO HOUSE Oyado Eleven
properties.description: Pilgrim hostel directly in front of Fujii-dera and a practical starting point for the Shōsan-ji climb. Henro Hub records washer, dryer, microwave, bicycles and Wi-Fi among its facilities.

properties.name: Fujii-dera Okunoin — Dainichi Nyorai Statue
properties.description: Fujii-dera's Okunoin on the ascent above Temple 11, recorded in Henro Hub as the Dainichi Nyorai Statue.

properties.name: Chōto-an
properties.description: A small Daishi-dō and traditional resting stop on the Shōsan-ji approach, associated with a Kōbō Daishi statue. Henro Hub records a toilet at the site.

properties.name: The birthplace of landscape
properties.description: A quiet mountain-trail rest hut and viewpoint with a wide bench and expansive scenery. Henro Hub records no nearby services.

properties.name: Ryusui-an
properties.description: A sacred stop on the Shōsan-ji approach where several small structures once served as pilgrim shelters. Henro Hub's Shōsan-ji research also records fresh water here.

properties.name: Pilgrim Rest Area Ryūsui-an
properties.description: An enclosed pilgrim hut in the forest beside Ryūsui-an, with space for roughly three to four people and usually spring water. No toilet is recorded.

properties.name: Joren-an
properties.description: Also known as Ipponsugian, a sacred roadside stop associated with a large cedar traditionally believed to have been planted by Kōbō Daishi and with a Daishi statue.

properties.name: Joshin-an
properties.description: A small hall or hermitage on the Shōsan-ji approach associated with Jizō worship and training practice. Henro Hub notes that it is not formally Shōsan-ji's Okunoin.

properties.name: Ryūō-kutsu
properties.description: A sacred cave associated with dragon-king (Ryūō) belief on the mountain. Henro Hub notes that it is not the formal Okunoin of Shōsan-ji.

properties.name: Shōsan-ji
properties.description: Temple 12 of the Shikoku 88-temple pilgrimage, dramatically situated more than 700 metres above sea level on a forested mountain ridge. It is the first major nansho, or hard-to-reach sacred site, of the route.

properties.name: Zaō-Dai Gongen
properties.description: Shōsan-ji's summit Okunoin, preserving the mountain-cult and Shugendō layer of the sacred landscape. It is reached by a steep continuation beyond Temple 12.
